author: rgdevment
description: Local memory and context for you and your AI agent, in Tisty on your own disk, for Windows and macOS. Your assistant picks up where it left off, files tasks with steps and dates, keeps a dated journal, writes and edits documents passage by passage, reads them by outline and section, jots and sorts ideas on Brainstorm, and searches past work over local stdio, with no account or server; it never closes or deletes anything.
name: Tisty

prompts.name: pick_up
prompts.title: Pick up where I left off
prompts.description: What moved since last time, then the open task last worked on and its latest notes.

arguments.name: task
arguments.description: A word from the task to pick up; left out, the one last worked on

prompts.name: leave_off
prompts.title: Leave this where I can pick it up
prompts.description: Tick what is finished and note what was done, ruled out and comes next, so the next session starts from there.

arguments.name: task
arguments.description: A word from the task to leave; left out, the one we are on

prompts.name: plan_task
prompts.title: Plan this work as a task with steps
prompts.description: One task with its steps in its list, once no task already covers it.

arguments.name: work
arguments.description: What is to be done; left out, what we have been talking about

prompts.name: solved_before
prompts.title: How did we solve this before?
prompts.description: Search the archive of finished tasks and the documents before trying anything new.

arguments.name: problem
arguments.description: A word for the problem; left out, the one we are on

prompts.name: keep_decision
prompts.title: Keep this decision in its document
prompts.description: Write the decision just made into the one document on its subject, in place.

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: What the decision is about; left out, plain from the conversation

prompts.name: brainstorm
prompts.title: Brainstorm ideas with me
prompts.description: Think up short ideas on a subject together, and jot on Brainstorm the ones I keep.

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: What the ideas are about; left out, what we have been talking about

prompts.name: sort_ideas
prompts.title: Sort out my Brainstorm
prompts.description: Group the ideas waiting on Brainstorm and propose which become tasks, which go into documents and which are marked as old.

arguments.name: subject
arguments.description: A word for the ideas to sort; left out, all of them

resources.name: document
resources.title: A document, or some of its lines
resources.description: A document by its id. A long one comes as its outline; `from` and `to` read the lines between.

tools.name: propose
tools.title: Propose a task
tools.description: Propose a task, something to do; what is kept to read again is `write_doc`. Several from one thread go in `tasks`, each judged alone. Work of several tasks with one end goes in `parts`, not packed into steps. An idea named as `source` leaves Brainstorm. Tisty tags it #agent.

again.description: Only when the person asks in this conversation to redo what was filed from this source and closed since, never for one still open; say in the description how the last one ended

date.description: The day it is meant to be done, or with a deadline the day work starts (2026-08-31)

deadline.description: The day it truly runs out (2026-08-31); only then is it overdue

description.description: What you read, in the Tisty language

list.description: An existing list, by name, as `catch_up` names it. Left out, it lands in the inbox, which needs a reason

part_of.description: Id of an open task this one is a part of

parts.description: Its parts, each shaped like a single task with its own steps: one level, at most 32 here, more later with `part_of`

remind.description: When to ring, like 2026-08-30T20:00: only for a one-off at a set hour that cannot be caught up on, the evening before

source.description: Where you read it: a message id, a thread link

steps.description: A checklist, each step at most 100 characters; what needs more is a part

tags.description: Its subjects, one plain word each, reusing the tags `catch_up` shows; six is already a lot

tasks.description: Several tasks, each shaped like a single one, at most 32; left out for one

title.description: What has to be done, in a line

tools.name: remind
tools.title: Set a task to ring
tools.description: Make a task ring at given moments. It adds to what the task rings at and never removes a reminder (`read` shows them). Not for what repeats: a routine comes back on its own.

at.description: Each a day and an hour, like 2026-08-30T20:00

tools.name: describe
tools.title: Describe a task
tools.description: Write the description of an open task. It replaces the old one whole: `read` first and keep what holds; what you learnt goes in `note`.

body.description: What the task is, in the Tisty language

tools.name: plan
tools.title: Add steps to a task
tools.description: Add steps to an open task, after those already there (`read` shows them). One done on its own is a part: `propose` with `part_of`.

steps.description: The steps to add, in order, each at most 100 characters

tools.name: tick
tools.title: Tick the steps you did
tools.description: Tick steps you did yourself, by their text, as you finish each. All or nothing: one unknown text ticks none; a text two steps share ticks the next open one. On the person's own tasks it reports the step done, for them to confirm. Refused once the task is said done: `note` instead. The whole task is `say_done`; a wrong tick, `untick`.

steps.description: The steps you did, by their text as `read` shows it; case and accents do not matter

tools.name: untick
tools.title: Take back a tick given by mistake
tools.description: Take back a tick, or your word on a step, an agent gave by mistake. A tick the person gave is theirs, and naming it unticks nothing. It opens and closes nothing.

steps.description: The steps to untick, by their text as `read` shows it; case and accents do not matter

tools.name: rename
tools.title: Rename a task
tools.description: Retitle a task when the title no longer says what it is. Steps are `reword_step`, and the page `describe` or `edit_doc`.

tools.name: reword_step
tools.title: Rewrite an open step
tools.description: Rewrite an unticked step of an open task. A ticked step is refused: `untick` it first if your tick was a mistake.

step.description: The step, by its text as `read` shows it

text.description: What the step says now, at most 100 characters

tools.name: unplan
tools.title: Take open steps off a task
tools.description: Take unticked steps off an open task. With `to` they are handed on, after that task's own steps, instead of dropped. One ticked step among them and nothing changes.

steps.description: The steps to take off, by their text as `read` shows it; case and accents do not matter

to.description: Id of another open task, not said done, to hand them to

tools.name: move
tools.title: Hang a task under another, or move it to a list
tools.description: `part_of` hangs a task under another, or null lets it stand alone; `list` moves it to a better list. One level: a task with parts is no part. A closed task takes nothing; a whole said done or not doing takes no new part.

list.description: An existing list, by name, as `catch_up` names it

part_of.description: Id of the task to hang it under, or null to let it go

tools.name: reword_note
tools.title: Rewrite a note in a task's journal
tools.description: Rewrite a note in the journal of an open task, named by the id `read` shows beside it. The new body replaces it whole and cannot be empty. To add one, `note`.

body.description: What the note says now, in the Tisty language

tools.name: note
tools.title: Add to a task's journal
tools.description: Add to a task's journal, the person's tasks too, when something new turns up about existing work, instead of filing a duplicate. A closed task takes none: propose the work anew. A note inside a document is a callout (`> [!NOTE]`), with `edit_doc`.

body.description: What to record, in the Tisty language

tools.name: attach
tools.title: Attach a file to a task or a document
tools.description: Copy a file from this machine into Tisty: with `task` onto its journal, with `doc` at the end of that document as a picture or a card. Up to 650 MB; an HTML page is kept, never run. Attach only what you were asked to.

doc.description: The document's id, to add it there

label.description: What to call it; defaults to the file's name

path.description: A file under Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Desktop or the temporary folder

task.description: The task id, to keep it with a task

tools.name: write_doc
tools.title: Write a document
tools.description: Write a document, something kept and read again; work to do is `propose`. Markdown is turned into the Tisty language and `turned` says what changed. Alone it writes a new one: `find` first, as a subject with a document is updated there, and a title in use is refused. With `doc` and `print` it rewrites that one whole, page lines the body drops going back at the end; one passage is `edit_doc`. #words in its text tag it.

anyway.description: Write it although a document names the same subject; only when it truly is another

body.description: The whole document; its first line is its title. One line per paragraph: a single newline is a line break, so wrapped text reads broken

compact.description: With `doc` and `print`: this write puts the document back in order, as `rules` «tidying» says. Refused on one the person began unless `person_asked`

doc.description: Id of a document to write again whole, not its title; needs `print`. Left out, a new one

folder.description: The existing folder its subject belongs in, by name, path or id; left out needs a reason. Not with `doc`: `file_doc` moves one

lang.description: With `translation_of`: the body's language tag, like `es`, `en` or `pt-BR`

page_of.description: Id of the document this is a page of: it is named at that document's end (`page_doc` moves the line), takes its folder and holds no pages

person_asked.description: With `compact`: the person asked you in this conversation to compact a document they began

print.description: The `print` `read_doc` gave with the text you worked from; if the document changed since, nothing is written

translation_of.description: Id of a document this one says in another language, joined as one more of its languages; both say their language, in `lang` or a `lang:` property

tools.name: append_doc
tools.title: Add to a document, or to a task's page
tools.description: Add at a document's end, or under the heading in `under`, without reading it or a `print`; nothing written changes, unless `replace` rewrites a task page's assistant notes. For logs, minutes and dated notes; a changed fact is `edit_doc`. The answer says how much it `grew`. A task's id in `doc` adds under the assistant's notes on its page, dated and signed.

body.description: Markdown to add, after a blank line

doc.description: A document's id, not its title, or a task's to add to its page

echo.description: Hand back the lines around the change, instead of reading again

replace.description: Only with a task's id: rewrite the assistant's notes on its page whole, as one dated digest; a box in it is no step

under.description: A heading, as it reads: adds at the end of what it holds. Left out, at the end of the document

tools.name: restore_doc
tools.title: Put a document back the way it was
tools.description: Undo the last write to a document: a changed passage or a whole write is put back; appends and the person's saves keep nothing to undo. Refused if written since, unless `even_if_more`. Undoing twice returns it. Use it when a write answers something unexpected, instead of retyping.

doc.description: A document's id, not its title, or a task's to put back the assistant's notes on its page

even_if_more.description: Go back over what was written since too; only once you read it and know, since the person may have written it

tools.name: edit_doc
tools.title: Change a passage of a document
tools.description: Replace one passage of a document, named by its text in `old` or by place with `section` or `from` and `to`, which needs no reading of the rest. What it said is kept first for `restore_doc`, or the edit is refused. The answer's `grew` should be close to what you sent. A task's page too, by its own name: its boxes are the task's steps.

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

echo.description: Hand back the lines around the change, instead of reading again

from.description: First line to replace, from 1. Needs `print`

new.description: What takes its place; empty takes the passage out

old.description: The passage as written now, from `read_doc`, matching one place only; take in a line around it if needed. Not with `section` or lines

print.description: The `print` from `read_doc` or `outline_doc`, for `section` or lines only. If anyone wrote since, nothing changes: ask `outline_doc` again

section.description: A heading and all under it, by its `at` in the `outline` of `outline_doc`, from 0. Needs `print`

to.description: Last line; left out, to the end. Only with `from`

tools.name: edit_table
tools.title: Change a table in a document
tools.description: Read or change one table of a document by rows and columns, never its Markdown; without `do` it only shows the table. A row is named by its first cell, a column by its title, as `show` gives them. Values are written as the column's type reads them (1234.5, 2026-10-28, true); one that does not fit is kept and named.

column.description: For set, sort, type, rename and remove_column: its title, or its number from 1

do.description: Defaults to show: the columns with their types and the rows, changing nothing

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

row.description: For set and remove: its first cell's words, or its number from 1

table.description: Its number from 1, or the heading over it. Left out when there is one

title.description: For rename and add_column: the column's title

type.description: For type and add_column: as written in braces in its head, like `number`, `money USD sum`, `date`, `check` (`language` «tables»); empty removes it

value.description: For set: what goes in the cell; empty clears it

values.description: For add: each column's title with its value; columns left out stay empty

tools.name: docs
tools.title: The documents and the folders
tools.description: The documents, newest first, with each one's folder, whether it is put away or locked, and what it holds (words, sections, key words): enough to pick one unopened. A task's words come with the task. Ask before writing, so nothing is kept twice.

after.description: Skip this many, to page on while `total` is higher

deep.description: With `folder`: the folders below it too

folder.description: Only the documents in this folder, by name, path or id, without pages; the folders below are named under `below`

folders.description: Every folder too, with id, path, icon and size; the text already names them

page_of.description: Only the pages of this document, by id, in reading order

tools.name: import_doc
tools.title: Bring a Markdown file in as a document
tools.description: Bring one Markdown file from disk in as a document, turned into the Tisty language, saying what changed. Files it points at come in too; links to what cannot are taken out. The file on disk is untouched; a seeming live credential comes in under a warning. A task's exported page goes back to its task. One file per call.

anyway.description: Bring it in although a document has the same subject; only when it truly is another

folder.description: The existing folder its subject belongs in, by name, path or id. Left out needs a reason

page_of.description: Id of the document it becomes a page of

path.description: A Markdown file under Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Desktop or the temporary folder

title.description: A title for a file whose first line is not one; defaults to the file name

tools.name: export_doc
tools.title: Export a document to a folder
tools.description: Write a document out as Markdown files in a folder on this machine, its pages numbered in reading order and its files beside them. A copy: nothing here changes. For another tool, `read_doc` with `as`.

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

into.description: An existing folder under Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Desktop or the temporary folder, not used for this document before

tools.name: archive_doc
tools.title: Put a document away, or bring it back
tools.description: Put a document or one page away when the person asks, or bring it back with `archived` false; nothing is deleted or changed («delete it» is `flag_doc`). A page put away stays under its document, read-only; a document's pages go and come back with it.

archived.description: True, the default, puts it away; false brings it back

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

folder.description: A folder to file it in on the way, by name, path or id

tools.name: flag_doc
tools.title: Mark a document that had its day
tools.description: Mark what had its day, or «delete this document»: the person deletes it, puts it away or unmarks it. Give the `reason`, `instead` where its content lives now, and `body`. Copies go in one call: one click deletes or unmarks them all. A document already marked is refused, or skipped in a set.

body.description: In the person's language: what makes it old, and how you know

doc.description: The id of the document to mark, not its title, or `sheet#heading` for an idea; a list is marked alike

instead.description: Id of the document or task that holds it now; needed with duplicate_of, moved and superseded

reason.description: A copy of another, moved into another (only once what it held worth keeping is there), superseded by another, wrong, obsolete, or a scratch nobody needs

tools.name: file_doc
tools.title: Put documents in a folder
tools.description: Move documents into a folder, or out of every folder by leaving `folder` out. Only the place changes; an archived document moves and stays put away.

doc.description: The id of the document to file, not its title, or a list of ids: if one cannot, none moves

folder.description: An existing folder, by name, path or id

tools.name: page_doc
tools.title: Make pages, put them in order, or take one out
tools.description: Hang a document under another as a page, or with no `page_of` take a page back out to its old folder. A page goes everywhere with its document. Hanging writes the line naming it at the document's end, or where `after`, `before` or `at` say; taking out leaves the line for you to remove. `order` reorders a document's pages. Reading order is line order, each line `![Its title](tisty:doc/its-id)`, bang included.

after.description: Id of another page of that document, whose line this one's goes right after. Needs `page_of` and one `doc`, and that page needs a line

at.description: Before or after every page line, for when there is no page to name

doc.description: The id of the document to hang or take out, not its title, or a list of ids: if one cannot, none moves

order.description: Its pages' ids, two or more, each once, in reading order: their lines trade places, nothing else moves. With `page_of` alone; each needs a line

page_of.description: Id of the document it becomes a page of. Left out, it becomes a document of its own

tools.name: tongue_doc
tools.title: Join or leave a document's languages
tools.description: With `of`, join `doc` to that document's languages, moving it to its folder; without, take `doc` out of its languages. Both say their language in a `lang:` property, or `lang` for `doc`. A new translation is `write_doc` with `translation_of`.

doc.description: Id of the document to join or take out, not its title

lang.description: The language of `doc`, like `es`, `en` or `pt-BR`, when its properties lack one

of.description: Id of a document whose languages it joins. Left out, it leaves its own

tools.name: folder
tools.title: Make a folder
tools.description: Make a folder for documents (tasks go in lists), with an icon and colour if they fit. A name in use hands back that folder, found at any depth unless `inside` says where; an icon or colour sent restyles it.

color.description: red, orange, amber, green, teal, blue, indigo, purple, pink, brown or gray

icon.description: One emoji, or a drawn name: home, work, money, study, travel, health, food, family, code and the like

inside.description: An existing folder to nest it in, by name, path or id; four deep at most

name.description: Its own name, a word or two, at most 40 characters; a path only to say where to nest it, every step but the last existing

tools.name: read_doc
tools.title: Read a document, or a part of one
tools.description: A document's text and the `print` it reads at. Past about 12,000 characters it comes back as its outline (`whole` false): then ask for a `section`, lines, or `chars` at a time. Every part brings the print, so `edit_doc` needs no whole read.

as.description: The whole document in GitHub Markdown for another tool; tell the person what `left_out` lists (`rules` «documents»). Not with `section`, lines or `chars`

chars.description: About how many characters to bring; the answer gives `next` when there is more

cursor.description: The `next` a previous answer gave, with `chars`

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

print.description: The `print` the previous part came with; only with `cursor`

section.description: A heading and all under it, by its `at` in `outline_doc`, from 0

to.description: Last line; left out, to the end

tools.name: catch_up
tools.title: Where things stand, and what has moved
tools.description: Where things stand: lists, folders, top tags, counts, pressing tasks, newest documents, a `cursor`; what others moved since your last `catch_up`; `last`, the open task you were on. Ask it first.

since.description: A `cursor` from a previous `catch_up`, to count from there instead: it only reads, and brings your own changes too

tools.name: reschedule
tools.title: Move the day of a task an agent filed
tools.description: Change the `date` or `deadline` of a task an agent filed, when what you learnt moves it. A day the person set is theirs. Null takes a day off; nothing else changes.

date.description: The day it is to be done, or with a deadline the day work starts (2026-08-31); null takes it off

deadline.description: The day it is owed by; null takes it off

tools.name: say_done
tools.title: Say a task is finished
tools.description: Say a task is done when you did the work, in the turn it ends; on any task, as your word. Refused while a step is unticked or a part open and unmarked. What stopped mattering is `say_not_doing`. Nothing closes: the person decides. Say it once; news after goes in `note`.

body.description: What you did and what makes you sure (the command and its answer, the commit), in the Tisty language

tools.name: say_not_doing
tools.title: Say a task should not be done
tools.description: Say a task should not be done, on any task, as your word: it stopped mattering or became moot. Unticked steps do not stop it. Nothing drops: the person decides. Say it once; news after goes in `note`.

body.description: Why it should not be done, and what you found that says so, in the Tisty language

tools.name: sum_up
tools.title: Say what a document is about
tools.description: Leave a `summary` and `notes` on a document for the next agent, kept on this machine only and unseen by the person; a later write marks it stale. Write it after reading a long document, never instead, saying what it says.

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

notes.description: What working with it needs: which section holds what, what is stale or missing

summary.description: What it says and what a reader comes to it for, in a few lines

tools.name: outline_doc
tools.title: What is in a document
tools.description: A document's headings with their `at`, lines and size, its length and `print`, and its pages with title, length and sections: a few hundred tokens. Ask it first for a long document or a change in part. Also `pointed_at` (who links here), `by` (agent or person) and the signs it wants compacting: `alike`, `repeated`, `dead`, `mislabeled`, `loose`.

doc.description: The document's id from `docs`, not its title

tools.name: read
tools.title: Read a whole task
tools.description: Everything a task holds: steps, its `document` page with the description and your notes, the latest journal notes (ids for `reword_note`) and who wrote them, parts and files. Read it before noting or mending; `fields` narrows it. A closed task comes with `closed` and a `notice`: it is history, and nothing on it changes.

fields.description: Only these keys of the answer; the id always comes

notes.description: How many latest journal notes, each cut at 4000 chars; 0: all, whole

tools.name: find
tools.title: Search tasks and documents, archive included
tools.description: Search open and archived tasks and documents: words in `query`, the task fields below to sift, `source` to see if something was filed, `doc` for lines inside one document. A task matched in its page, steps or notes brings the `line`. Open a task hit with `read`, a document hit with `read_doc`.

after.description: Skip this many tasks, to page on while `total` is higher. Documents are not paged: `docsTotal` counts them

around.description: With `doc`: lines each side of a hit, 0 to 10, 1 by default

by_agent.description: True: filed by an agent; false: by the person

doc.description: Search inside this document: lines with every word, their numbers, neighbours cut at 200 characters, and section

folder.description: Only documents in this folder or below, by name, path or id

from.description: Date or deadline on or after this day (2026-08-31)

from_source.description: Tasks whose `source` starts with this, however written: «sereno» brings all read from there

list.description: In this list, as `catch_up` names it

part_of.description: Only the parts of this task, by id

query.description: Words that must all turn up, in any order, accents or not (with `doc`, on one line); quote a phrase. Not needed when sifting

said_done.description: True: an agent said done or not doing and the person has not decided; false: nobody did

scope.description: Defaults to either: open and archived together

source.description: Whether this exact source was filed already; not with `query`

tag.description: Carrying this tag, # or not. Any sifting field leaves documents out

to.description: Date or deadline on or before this day

tools.name: rules
tools.title: The rules for working here, by topic
tools.description: The rules for working here, one guide at a time; alone, the basics and an index. Ask the one the instructions name before a first write of its kind.

topic.description: The guide; left out, the basics and the index

tools.name: language
tools.title: What Tisty adds to Markdown
tools.description: Reference for the Markdown extensions Tisty reads, to look up before writing one: pens, underline, icons, callouts, folds, tags, cards, attachments, diagrams. Plain Markdown needs none. Without `topic`, the index; then ask only the topic you will write. How the app works is `help`.

topic.description: One part, named as the index names it, or all

tools.name: help
tools.title: How Tisty itself works
tools.description: Tisty's own Help pages, for when the person asks how Tisty does something: installing, tasks, documents, sync, encryption, assistants, shortcuts, privacy. Alone, the index; `topic` gives a page.

topic.description: One page, named as the index names it in either language

localizations.name: Tisty
localizations.description: Memoria y contexto locales para ti y tu agente de IA, en Tisty y en tu propio disco, para Windows y macOS. Tu asistente retoma donde quedó, anota tareas con pasos y fechas, lleva una bitácora con fechas, escribe y corrige documentos por pasajes, los lee por índice y sección, anota y ordena ideas en la Lluvia de ideas, y busca trabajo pasado por stdio local, sin cuenta ni servidor; nunca cierra ni borra nada.

deploymentOptions.description: The tisty-mcp launcher finds the Tisty app installed on this computer and starts its own MCP server over stdio.

setupSteps: Install Tisty: from the Microsoft Store or `winget install rgdevment.Tisty` on Windows, or `brew tap rgdevment/tap && brew trust rgdevment/tap && brew install --cask tisty` on macOS.
Open Tisty once. Settings › Assistants keeps the door for assistants open or closed.

systemDependencies.name: node
systemDependencies.description: Runs the tisty-mcp launcher through npx.

systemDependencies.name: tisty
systemDependencies.description: The free Tisty app for Windows or macOS, whose own server the launcher starts.

installInstructions.macos: brew tap rgdevment/tap && brew trust rgdevment/tap && brew install --cask tisty
